observations.NEUTRAL: Smooth, curved and strongly varying ribbon section; source geometry itself dominates the silhouette.
observations.FORMED: Actual cached formed geometry shows longitudinal grooves and local transverse kinks/rises on the ribbon. Broad deep enclosed coffer compartments and a clear serial node/neck structure are not strongly established before adding the carrier residual.
observations.CARRIER: The true G7 native patch differs from the neutral scaffold in larger bulges and section orientation, as well as local corrugations. This is not solely a fine texture difference.
observations.DELIVERED: The delivered geometry retains some formed ridge/groove changes but also inherits carrier bulges, local clumps and corrugations. It does not reveal a previously bold clean coffer chain.

causal_interpretation: A carrier-residual-only explanation is insufficient: the actual formed absolute geometry is already weak in the intended coffer morphology.

The carrier-minus-neutral difference visibly contributes further shape changes. It includes generation/carrier geometry and normal differences; no frequency decomposition has proved it is only fine residual.
Numerical differential pocket depth is not an absolute geometric pocket certificate on a convex, curved source section.
limitations: One intrinsic representative three-cell component40 interval was selected near median nominal height/base. This is an engineering diagnosis, not a beauty-selected region or whole-column verdict.
NEUTRAL/FORMED use actual cached local CC quad fans. CARRIER/DELIVERED use exact original native fan subsets with intentionally different topology.
Jagged open patch boundaries belong to extraction and are not counted as newly generated defects.
This alternate local intrinsic view does not reverse the rejected fixed whole-column close result or prove self-intersection absence.
next_requirement: Establish visibly adequate absolute formed section and connected compartment mass on the actual curved source before any further full-column generation; assess actual-carrier normal/section compatibility separately.
